insights.headline: Gold sinks to a seven-week low as surging oil and 5.2% Treasury yields fuel Fed rate-hike bets
insights.summary: Gold fell as much as 4% to about $4,111 an ounce on Monday, its lowest since early August, while silver slid over 5% to near $60.60. On MCX, gold futures dropped Rs 3,214 to Rs 1,47,667 per 10 grams and silver Rs 6,661 to Rs 2,28,035 per kg, with Delhi silver plunging Rs 5,000 to Rs 2.32 lakh. Brent crude surging past $108 on the US-Iran impasse and US borrowing costs at multi-decade highs have markets pricing roughly 70% odds of another Fed hike in October. Indian festive buyers are holding back until prices stabilise, though analysts point to central-bank buying and Diwali demand as support.
points: Spot gold fell up to 4% to $4,111/oz, its lowest since early August, as the US 10-year yield touched its highest since 2007.
MCX gold futures slid Rs 3,214 to Rs 1,47,667/10g; silver fell Rs 6,661 to Rs 2,28,035/kg, with Delhi silver down Rs 5,000 to Rs 2.32 lakh.
Brent surged past $108 after Trump rejected Iran's proposal, stoking inflation fears and bets on more Fed tightening.
Festive and wedding buyers are deferring purchases until prices stabilise, IBJA's Surendra Mehta said.
CFTC data showed money managers' net gold longs at their lowest since late July; gold ETFs saw 1.6 tonnes of weekly outflows.

trending.title: The bond-market rout is running the show
trending.summary: Multi-decade highs in US borrowing costs have crushed non-yielding bullion, dragging spot gold to $4,111 and silver toward $60.60, with analysts warning of further pressure until yields cool.

trending.title: Indian buyers go on a buying strike
trending.summary: With Diwali weeks away, jewellers say customers are waiting out the fall rather than buying the dip, and gold-silver ETFs tumbled over 4%. Demand isn't gone — it's paused.

trending.title: Silver takes the harder hit
trending.summary: Silver's 5%+ single-day fall outpaced gold as industrial exposure and thin liquidity amplified the selloff. Yet UBS still sees $80 by September 2027 on gold and industrial demand.

trending.title: Oil and the rupee tighten the squeeze
trending.summary: Brent above $108 is pressuring the rupee toward 96 to the dollar and pushing Indian bond yields to a 2.5-year peak — a double hit for domestic gold pricing.

trending.title: China: the demand anchor to watch
trending.summary: China remains on pace to import 1,700 tonnes of gold in 2026 even as premiums fade into the holiday week, while its big banks are shutting retail investors out of leveraged gold and silver futures.

items.title: Gold tumbles 4% to seven-week low as oil, dollar and yields climb
items.summary: Gold fell 4% on Monday to a seven-week low as surging oil prices revived inflation fears and hardened bets on further Fed tightening. Spot gold touched $4,110.55 — its lowest since August 5 — while silver dropped 4.5% to $61.39. A near-two-month-high dollar and climbing Treasury yields added pressure, and traders now price about 94% odds of a December Fed hike.

items.title: Gold price falls Rs 2,600, silver plunges Rs 5,000 on Monday
items.summary: In Delhi, gold of 99.9% purity fell Rs 2,600 to Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams and silver plunged Rs 5,000 to Rs 2.32 lakh per kg, tracking a global selloff as Brent surged past $108 and the dollar held firm. Overseas, spot gold slid 3% to $4,156 an ounce and silver 4.6% to $61.34.

items.title: Gold, silver slide as buyers wait for prices to stabilise
items.summary: MCX silver futures fell Rs 6,661 to Rs 2,28,035 per kg and gold slipped Rs 3,214 to Rs 1,47,667 per 10 grams on Monday. Kolkata jewellers said festive and wedding buyers are deferring purchases until prices stabilise, with IBJA's Surendra Mehta noting buying usually happens in rising markets, not falling ones.

items.title: Gold's lustre dims as Treasury yields surge, markets bet on higher Fed rates
items.summary: Spot gold fell as much as 4% to $4,111 an ounce, its lowest since early August, as the US 10-year Treasury yield touched its highest since 2007 and markets priced a roughly 70% chance of another Fed hike in October. CFTC data showed money managers' net gold longs at their lowest since late July, while Chinese premiums faded to zero ahead of the holiday week.

Indian gold and silver ETFs tumbled up to 4% on Monday, mirroring the sharp fall in bullion as Fed rate-hike bets strengthened. The slide tracked MCX futures lower, with higher US yields and a firm dollar cited as the immediate triggers.
items.title: Why Gold, silver ETFs tumbled over 4% today | What's behind the fall and what should investors do?
Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD drops to near $60.50 amid surging oil, Treasury yields
items.summary: Silver extended its slide in Asian trade on Tuesday, hovering near $60.60 an ounce after losing over 5% in the previous session, as elevated oil prices and fresh multi-year highs in Treasury yields fed expectations of more Fed tightening. Markets are pricing roughly 70% odds of an October rate hike, with US PCE and payrolls data due this week.

items.title: China on pace to import 1,700 tonnes of gold in 2026, silver price faces key test near $60/oz – Heraeus
items.summary: China’s gold imports reached 1,141 tonnes in the first eight months of 2026, already above all of 2025, and are on pace for about 1,700 tonnes – the highest of the decade – driven by investment demand, according to Heraeus analysts cited by Kitco. The note adds that silver faces a key test near $60 an ounce.

items.title: Gold correction approaches a critical support test as longer-term upside targets remain intact
items.summary: Kitco's technical analysis sees gold approaching a critical support test near $4,100.68, with a deeper $3,947-$3,887 zone below if that fails. A confirmed low at either level could keep longer-term upside targets of $4,550 to $5,368 in play.

items.title: Crude oil worries drag rupee, push bond yields to fresh 2.5-year peak
items.summary: India's 10-year bond yield rose 6 bps to 7.19% on Monday, a 2.5-year high, with the 5-year yield up to 6.88%, as crude near $107 and a weaker rupee pressured markets. The rupee fell to 95.99 per dollar and is down 6.37% this year. Yields rose despite strong demand at the RBI's final Rs 25,000 crore bond sale, which drew Rs 67,655 crore in bids and took September OMO sales to Rs 1 trillion.

items.title: India Gold market cautiously optimistic with approach of festive and wedding seasons
items.summary: India's gold market is entering the festive and wedding season with cautious optimism, Money Metals reports: high prices have slowed discretionary jewellery buying, but wedding-related demand stays resilient. Indian gold ETF inflows rose sharply in August, digital gold buying stayed strong, and the World Gold Council expects steady investment buying.

items.title: How gold sector is gearing up $100 bn export target as India eyes massive expansion in $55 bn FTA jewellery market
items.summary: India's gems and jewellery industry is targeting $100 billion in exports, WGC India CEO Sachin Jain said at the Delhi Jewellery & Gem Fair. Jain added that 20-25% of India's gold consumption could come from domestic mines within five to seven years. FTA partner countries import $55 billion of jewellery a year while India's share is $8 billion.

UBS expects silver to recover to $70 an ounce by December 2026 and reach $80 by September 2027, via $75 in March and June 2027, citing support from higher gold prices and tighter near-term physical fundamentals — while cautioning that a more hawkish Fed remains a near-term headwind.
items.title: Silver Could Reach $80 by September 2027, According to UBS Forecast
Big Chinese banks ending retail leveraged gold and silver futures trading
items.summary: A dozen-plus large Chinese banks plan to end retail leveraged gold and silver futures trading, shutting down Shanghai Gold Exchange margin-traded Au(T+D) and Ag(T+D) contracts, Money Metals reports. China Everbright Bank will exit after October 19, joining ICBC, Bank of China and China Construction Bank. The shift could steer Chinese retail demand toward physical metal and ETFs.
